observations.title: sidecar jobId 検証の表現が既存 job-wait と差異
observations.rationale: request は「cancel の pid 解決を job wait と同じ連鎖に揃える」と表現しているが、現状 job-wait の realReadSidecarPid は jobId を検証しない。要件が要求する jobId-validated 版は cancel に追加する新しい安全ガードであり、既存 job-wait ロジックの単純な流用ではない。受け入れ基準は正確なので実装に影響しないが、design 段階で整合を確認すること。

observations.title: process group leader 判定の platform API が Bun/Node.js に存在しない
observations.rationale: POSIX での getpgid(pid) === pid 判定は Node.js/Bun 組み込み API では不可能。request は適切に design へ委ねているが、設計では ps -o pgid= サブプロセス呼び出しかサイドカーへの isGroupLeader フラグ追記など、実装アプローチの選択が必要になる。

toolResult.reason: Wrote design.md, spec.md, tasks.md under specrunner/changes/cancel-process-tree-kill/. Design captures the 5 architect-approved decisions (jobId-gated shared pid resolver, process-death-gate replacing status gate, leader-gated group SIGKILL via kill(-pid,0) probe, runner-owned QueryAbortHub abort seam reusing the per-call AbortController, output changes), with rationale + rejected alternatives, risks, and open questions. Spec has 5 SHALL/MUST requirements with Given/When/Then scenarios mapping every acceptance criterion. Tasks T-01..T-09 are granular with file paths and per-task acceptance criteria; existing pinned cancel suites kept green (isGroupLeader optional-with-default, 'no PID recorded' substring preserved, running-path SIGTERM preserved). Scope-outs respected; adapter→core/port boundary respected; ADR path left to adr-gen.

findings.title: bounded drain タイムアウトパスの scenario 欠落

findings.title: group kill エラー時の動作に normative 記述がない

findings.title: Group SIGKILL fires on SIGTERM-success polling path, not only at SIGKILL escalation
findings.rationale: reapGroup() is invoked at lines 103 and 110 (when the pid dies from SIGTERM during polling) in addition to the SIGKILL escalation block (lines 136-148). The spec says 'on SIGKILL escalation only' and the test scenarios (TC-006/TC-007) only cover the SIGKILL escalation path. For a dead group-leader pid whose descendants survive, isGroupLeader(dead_pid) = kill(-pid,0) succeeds → group SIGKILL is sent. groupKilled:true is then set, causing 'Process group reaped (SIGKILL sent to group)' in cancel output even when the runner itself only needed SIGTERM. Safety invariant holds (foreground jobs return false from isGroupLeader), but the SIGTERM-success group-kill path is untested.

options.label: Accept current behaviour (broader than spec, functionally correct)
options.consequence: SIGTERM-success + surviving children → group SIGKILL; cleaner than spec requires; groupKilled:true message on this path may mislead but causes no harm. No spec or test change needed.

options.label: Restrict reapGroup to SIGKILL escalation path only
options.consequence: Poll-death paths return groupKilled:false; children that survived SIGTERM would NOT be reaped unless escalation fires; aligns with spec but reduces cleanup coverage. Requires removing reapGroup() from lines 103 and 110.

findings.title: Cancel of failed/terminated jobs now attempts kill via stale liveness sidecar — untested combination
findings.rationale: Before this change, state.status==='running' gate prevented kills for failed/terminated jobs. Now the gate is removed (design D2). For a failed job: state.pid=null (cleared in pipeline.ts:161) but the sidecar still has the dead runner's pid (sidecar is NOT cleaned up on failure, only on cancel/archive). resolveJobPid adopts the sidecar pid (same jobId). gracefulKill sends SIGTERM to the (possibly reused) pid. Dead pid → ESRCH → safe. Pid reused → kills unrelated process. runner-process-gate.test.ts covers status=running and status=awaiting-resume with non-null sidecar, but NOT status=failed + non-null sidecar. If a future status restriction is added, this path would silently stop working.

options.label: Accept current behaviour; add a test for status=failed + non-null sidecar
options.consequence: Pins the intended process-death-gate behaviour for all statuses including failed/terminated; makes the behaviour regression-proof. Minimal change: one extra it() in runner-process-gate.test.ts.

options.label: Accept current behaviour without additional test
options.consequence: Leaves the failed+stale-sidecar path untested; risk is low (ESRCH handles dead pids safely; pid reuse is rare) but the behaviour change from the pre-change invariant is unpinned.

findings.title: TC-016 implicit structural assumption changed: first await is now hub.drain(), not store.load()
findings.rationale: TC-016 verifies markSignalHandlerFired() is called before the first await by capturing isSignalHandlerFired() at store.load() time. After this change the signal handler structure is: markSignalHandlerFired() → hub.abortActive() → await hub.drain() → await store.load(). TC-016 still passes because the flag is set before any await. However, TC-016 does not verify that drain() precedes store.load(). The new ordering invariant is pinned by runner-abort-hub.test.ts (TC-008/009/010 + regression test), but TC-016's own scope no longer covers the full sequencing contract. A future edit that moves drain() to after store.load() would not be caught by TC-016.

findings.title: Poll-death ESRCH branch untested for group-leader: production isAlive throws ESRCH, all tests use returning-false isAlive
findings.rationale: Production `isAlive` in cancel.ts throws ESRCH when a pid is dead. `gracefulKill` catches this in the ESRCH branch (line 103) and calls `reapGroup(pid, kill, isGroupLeader)`. All F-001 unit tests and the TC-021 integration test use an `isAlive` that returns `false` (not throws), exercising only the `!alive` branch (line 110). No test covers ESRCH + isGroupLeader=true → groupKilled=true. If `reapGroup` were removed from the ESRCH branch while kept in the `!alive` branch, all tests would pass but production's primary happy path (runner exits cleanly after SIGTERM → ESRCH observed → group reaped) would silently break — exactly the orphan case this change was designed to prevent. The spec.md explicitly requires both paths: 'whether observed via isAlive returning false or via ESRCH'. Fix: add one unit test with `isAlive` throwing ESRCH and `isGroupLeader=true`, asserting `kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` and `groupKilled===true`.

observations.title: Integration test isAlive diverges from production wiring — exercises !alive branch, not ESRCH branch
observations.rationale: The integration test wires isAlive as a catching wrapper that returns false on ESRCH (`try { process.kill(pid,0); return true; } catch { return false; }`). Production cancel.ts wires isAlive as a throwing function (`process.kill(pid,0); return true;`). TC-021 therefore validates the `!alive` code path, not the ESRCH catch path that production will actually take when the runner dies from SIGTERM. Both paths call `reapGroup` identically, so the observable outcome is the same, but the test does not faithfully reproduce the production execution path.

observations.title: sidecarAbsPath variable shadowed in two inner if(slug) blocks
observations.rationale: runner.ts declares `const sidecarAbsPath` at line 362 (outer, nullable) then redeclares it inside two separate `if (slug)` blocks for deletion and purge. The inner declarations shadow the outer but compute the same path value (both correctly scoped to non-null slug). No invariant is broken; mentioned for maintenance clarity only.

observations.title: TC-016 comment says first await is store.load() but it is now hub.drain()
observations.rationale: The comment in the test docstring describes the old ordering (first await = store.load). The actual first await is now hub.drain(). The test invariant (markSignalHandlerFired before store.load) still holds because markSignalHandlerFired fires synchronously before hub.abortActive() and hub.drain(). Operator adjudicated this as F-003 (no action needed). Noted as observation only.
